title: Behold thy mother
hookLine: a title given by Paul VI at the Second Vatican Council, now a memorial on the Monday after Pentecost
carry: behold thy mother: mary mothers every disciple
last: MARY COMFORTS BECAUSE SHE STOOD AT THE CROSS.

lines: A FAMILY MADE AT THE CROSS.
cards: "Woman, behold thy son." Words from the cross, in John's Gospel. Jesus is dying, and below him stand two people: his mother, and the disciple the Gospel calls the one whom he loved.

He speaks to her first, then turns to the disciple: "Behold thy mother." And John adds a line that's easy to read past: "And from that hour, the disciple took her to his own." At the worst hour, a family is made.
Catholics hear that sentence reaching much further than one house.

teach.h: THE DISCIPLE STANDS FOR EVERY DISCIPLE.
teach.b: You met this title on day three hundred twenty-three; today, its story. Start with the disciple. John's Gospel never names him in that scene.
Catholics read that as an open door: the beloved disciple stands for every disciple, so behold thy mother is spoken to each of them.
Some Christians read the scene more simply, as a dying son making sure his mother is looked after. Catholics hold that reading too, and hear more in it. Next, the upper room.
In the Acts of the Apostles, after Jesus is taken up, his friends pray together, with one mind, with the women and with Mary, the mother of Jesus.
Then comes Pentecost, the coming of the Holy Spirit, sometimes called the Church's birthday.

teach.h: IN THE ROOM WHEN THE CHURCH IS BORN.
teach.b: So Mary is there at the birth of Jesus, and in the room when the Church is born. Then the title.

During the Second Vatican Council, Pope Paul the Sixth gave Mary the name Mother of the Church, and the Catechism puts it in one line: Mother of Christ, Mother of the Church. The Council holds two things together.
She is a member of the Church, a believer like the rest. And she mothers it. Last, the calendar.
Pope Francis made the title a memorial, on the Monday after Pentecost.
That turns the Church from an institution into something more like a crowded kitchen table: people who didn't choose each other, handed to one another, with a mother keeping an eye on them all.

how: Catholics keep the memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Mother of the Church, on the Monday after Pentecost, and the Litany of Loreto includes the invocation "Mother of the Church, pray for us."

in that scene, John's Gospel names the disciple at the cross
the Gospel calls him the disciple whom he loved. Catholics read him as standing for every disciple.
Catholic teaching puts Mary outside the Church, above it

games.q: you're the disciple at the cross. Jesus says to you, behold thy mother. what do you do?
o: nod, and go home alone afterward.
take her into your own home.
games.why: "and from that hour, the disciple took her to his own" (John 19:27). Catholics hear in it a family that reaches every disciple.

practice: Picture the Church not as a building but as a table full of people, starting with one parish you know, then widening: people who serve, people who are tired, people who were hurt, people who walked away, people gathering far off where it costs them.
If you pray, use the line Mother of the Church, pray for us, and leave them with her. If you don't, hold that crowded table and wish it well.

wordCard.voice: Mother of the Church. Mary's title from the Second Vatican Council, kept on the Monday after Pentecost: a member of the family, and the one who mothers it.

orig.note: Latin: Mother of the Church, the title Paul VI gave Mary.
